content:
Facts: Mother brought reduction action against son's widow (appointed universal heir by holographic will) receiving only usufruct bequest on apartment; non-definitive judgment ascertained legitimate portion infringement and estate composition; mother died during proceedings, replaced by daughter claiming heir status; division phase addressed property allocation, occupancy compensation claims, alleged exclusive enjoyment fruits, and monetary adjustment calculations.
Legal Framework: Articles 540(2), 544, 720, 728-729 Italian Civil Code (spousal habitation rights; ascendant-spouse competition; inconvenient divisibility; monetary adjustments); Arts. 167, 183(6), 273, 282, 302 Italian Code of Civil Procedure (late claims; modification deadlines; joinder; provisional enforcement; succession in proceedings); Art. 2697 (burden of proof).
Interpretive Issues: Whether procedural succession requires formal proof of heir status via civil registry documents or suffices through tacit acceptance and unopposed allegations; admissibility of occupancy compensation claim first raised in post-expert observations rather than introductory or modification phases; treatment of spousal habitation right value when universal heir receives property assignment; criteria for mandatory property allocation versus sale when co-heir requests assignment; revaluation necessity for monetary adjustments when no alleged market appreciation; provisional enforceability of adjustment payment pending constitutive division judgment finality.
Principles Applied: Procedural succession heir status proven through all acquired evidence, not exclusively civil registry documents; no legal proof requirement for heir status in civil system. Tacit acceptance inferred from resumption act alleging heir status; constitutes conclusive conduct establishing procedural relationship. Untimely generic objection to heir status in reply brief, absent prior challenge and after three-year continuation, deemed instrumental when defendant previously acknowledged family relationship. Occupancy compensation claim inadmissible when first raised post-modification deadline in expert observation brief; independent action requiring timely assertion despite divisional context. Exclusive property enjoyment by universal heir constitutes Art. 540(2) habitation/use right exercise; value already computed in share determination. Article 720 allocation mandatory when co-heir requests assignment and no other requests it; "preferably" refers to largest-share criterion, not allocation-versus-sale choice. Sale represents last resort only when all co-owners unwilling to acquire whole. Habitation right extinguishes by confusion upon full ownership attribution; separate transcription request rejected. Monetary adjustment debt not provisionally enforceable per Art. 282 pending constitutive allocation judgment finality; reciprocal albeit non-synallagmatic relationship. Adjustment revaluation denied absent alleged market appreciation proving disproportion since succession opening; burden on claimant. Late document production (closing brief attachments) inadmissible; supervening documents require production request when clarifying conclusions. Precautionary seizure declared ineffective subject to allocation judgment finality; ultra-effectiveness ceases when division constitutively attributes rights. Costs allocation reflects preliminary (reduction accepted) and merit (division unopposed) phases; expert costs allocated equally for joint-interest operations, proportionally for contested claims.
